title: Relative affine Tor bounds and pseudo-coherent diagonal finiteness
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of commutative rings, with $R$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Put $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, let $g:U\to V$ be the induced morphism, and put $B=A\otimes_R A$ [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $E\in D(\mathcal O_U)$ be pseudo-coherent [def-pc-derived-category], [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Assume that every point of $U$ has an open neighbourhood $T$ and integers $a_T\le b_T$ such that $H^i(E|_T\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{(g^{-1}\mathcal O_V)|_T}(g^{-1}\mathcal G)|_T)=0$ for every $\mathcal O_V$-module sheaf $\mathcal G$ and every $i\notin[a_T,b_T]$; derived tensors are computed by K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Then $E$ has quasi-coherent cohomology, and there exist $M\in D(A)$, an isomorphism $\widetilde M\cong E$ under [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], and integers $a\le b$ such that $M$ is pseudo-coherent over $A$ [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] and $H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every $R$-module $N$ and every $i\notin[a,b]$. In particular $H^i(M)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. The ring $B$ is Noetherian, and the $B$-module $A$, with action through $\mu:B\to A$, $x\otimes y\mapsto xy$, has a bounded-above finite-free resolution, so $A[0]$ is pseudo-coherent in $D(B)$. Moreover $B$ is flat over $A$ through $p_1:a\mapsto a\otimes1$; for $M_1=M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A,p_1}B$ its degree-zero flat representative $B[0]$ computes this tensor and there are natural isomorphisms $H^i(M_1)\cong H^i(M)\otimes_{A,p_1}B$ for all $i$. Thus $H^i(M_1)=0$ for $i<a$.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-pseudo-coherent-qcoh], the given pseudo-coherent $E$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. The equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] therefore supplies $M\in D(A)$ and $\widetilde M\cong E$. Apply [lem-pc-affine-pseudo-coherent-criterion] to a complex representing $M$: it is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $A$-modules. This is precisely pseudo-coherence of $M$ by [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex].

The affine $U$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Choose finitely many of the hypothesized neighbourhoods $T_j$ covering $U$, and put $a=\min_j a_{T_j}$ and $b=\max_j b_{T_j}$. If $U$ is empty, choose $a=b=0$; every module sheaf there is zero. Fix any base module sheaf $\mathcal G$. Compute $E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{g^{-1}\mathcal O_V}g^{-1}\mathcal G$ using a K-flat resolution over the ringed space $(U,g^{-1}\mathcal O_V)$, supplied by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Its restriction to $T_j$ remains K-flat, and restriction is exact, by [lem-sfb-ringed-site-restriction-kflat]. The natural sheaf tensor restriction isomorphism of [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction], applied in each degree against the degree-zero test sheaf, identifies the restricted tensor complex with the tensor computing the hypothesis on $T_j$. Thus its cohomology vanishes on every $T_j$ outside $[a,b]$. A sheaf zero on a covering is zero: any section restricts to zero on that cover and is zero by the separatedness axiom. Consequently the global inverse-image test holds in this single interval.

proof.text: Apply the fixed-interval assertion and inverse-image-test equivalence of [lem-trf-affine-relative-tor-amplitude-criterion] to $R\to A$, the affine model $M$ of Step 1 and the interval of Step 2. This gives $H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every $R$-module $N$ and every $i\notin[a,b]$. In particular take $N=R$. On the one-point ringed site, [lem-fd-ringed-flat-single-tensor-cohomology] with the free rank-one module $R$ computes $H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R)=H^i(M)\otimes_R R\cong H^i(M)$; the last map is $m\otimes r\mapsto rm$, inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. Hence $H^i(M)=0$ outside $[a,b]$.

source.place: Tag 0DHY (lemma-tor-dimension-rel-affine), part (1); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), flat-single specialization.

proof.text: Choose finite algebra generators $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ of $A$ over $R$ from its finite presentation. Then $x_i\otimes1$ and $1\otimes x_i$ generate $B$ as an $R$-algebra: every pure tensor is the product $(x\otimes1)(1\otimes y)$ and pure tensors generate the tensor product additively. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $B$ Noetherian. The multiplication map $\mu:B\to A$ is surjective since $\mu(x\otimes1)=x$, and $1\in A$ generates $A$ as a $B$-module: $x=(x\otimes1)\cdot1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-resolution-noetherian] with ring $B$ and this cyclic module. Put its terms $B^{n_j}$ in degrees $-j$ and zero in positive degrees. Exactness of the augmented resolution gives a quasi-isomorphism to $A[0]$. This is a bounded-above finite-free model, so [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] says that $A[0]$ is pseudo-coherent in $D(B)$. No finite length for the resolution is asserted.

The $R$-module $A$ is flat by hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] with $R'=A$ and $M=A$: $A\otimes_R A$ is flat as an $A$-module through the first tensor factor, exactly the specified $p_1$. On the one-point ringed site with coefficient ring $A$, specialize [lem-fd-ringed-flat-single-tensor-cohomology] to the flat module $L=B$. It says $B[0]$ is K-flat, computes $M_1=M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A,p_1}B$ by termwise flat tensor, and supplies $H^i(M_1)\cong H^i(M)\otimes_{A,p_1}B$ for every $i$, naturally in $M$. These maps are also $B$-linear: naturality in endomorphisms of the flat module $B$, applied to multiplication by each $c\in B$, intertwines the two $B$-actions. Thus these are the asserted scalar-extension cohomology isomorphisms. Step 3 and tensoring the zero module with $B$ now give $H^i(M_1)=0$ for $i<a$.
